title: Integral strict prime-power quotient completion is the orthogonal reflector
statement: For a prime ell and an arbitrary scheme W, fix an integral simultaneous quotient reduction I and any total right derived inverse limit RZ with its universal comparison, all in the universe conventions of [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface]. There is a natural unit Id to I.T followed by RZ. Its outputs receive only zero morphisms from any derived abelian sheaf on which ell acts invertibly. Precomposition by the unit is bijective on morphisms into every object with this orthogonality property. This concerns only integral sheaves and has no p-adic scalar extension, diagonal, Cartier boundary or cycle-class assertion.

source.place: Proof step 4, integral completion reflector; Stacks Tags 099M, 091S and 091Z

proof.text: Use the strict-model comparison to identify I.T followed by the specified total right derived inverse limit, after the exact additive integer-coefficient equivalence, with the source completion endofunctor.

Specialize the source principal completion adjunction to the lifted integers and the ideal generated by ell. Primality makes ell a nonzerodivisor. The source principal criterion identifies its complete objects with those right orthogonal to ell-invertible objects. Convert scalar multiplication by the integer cast of ell into repeated addition; the adjunction unit then has complete outputs and the required Hom bijection.

Transport this unit through the fully faithful derived coefficient equivalence and the natural comparison isomorphism. An additive equivalence preserves and reflects invertibility of ell times the identity and the orthogonality condition. Its Hom equivalences and the comparison isomorphism transport the adjunction bijection. Naturality follows by taking the fully faithful preimage of the conjugated natural transformation.

proof_origin.place: P3: source fixed-coefficient completion reflector plus strict-model comparison, Stacks 099M, 091S, 091Z. Generic additive-equivalence transport is proved in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem integral_strict_completion_reflector (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (W : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalAb W)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W)]
    (I : DiagonalDerivedReduction ℓ (𝟭 (DiagonalAb W)))
    (RZ : DerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W) ⥤ DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W))
    (ηZ : (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W) ⥤ DiagonalAb W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RZ)
    (hRZ : RZ.IsRightDerivedFunctor ηZ
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W) (.up ℤ))) :
    ∃ unit : 𝟭 (DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W)) ⟶ I.T ⋙ RZ,
      (∀ (K P : DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W)), IsIso (ℓ • 𝟙 P) →
        Subsingleton (P ⟶ (I.T ⋙ RZ).obj K)) ∧
      ∀ (K N : DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W)),
        (∀ P : DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W), IsIso (ℓ • 𝟙 P) → Subsingleton (P ⟶ N)) →
        Function.Bijective (fun f : (I.T ⋙ RZ).obj K ⟶ N ↦ unit.app K ≫ f)
